clauses.text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me as President of the 
United States, it is ordered that all lands 
owned or controlled by the United States 
within the following-described area, com­
prising 144.30 acres, more or less, in Ben­
son County, North Dakota, be, and they 
are hereby, reserved and set apart, sub­
ject to valid rights, for the use of the 
Department of Agriculture as a refuge 
and breeding ground for migratory birds 
and other wildlife:
Fifth Principal Meridian
T. 152 N., R. 65 W.,
sec. 12, lot 7 and SW%SE%; 
sec. 13, lot 1 and NW % NE^.
It is unlawful for any person to pursue, 
hunt, trap, capture, wilfully disturb, or 
kill any bird or wild animal of any kind 
whatsoever within the limits of the ref­
uge, or to enter thereon, except under 
such rules and regulations as may be pre­
scribed by the Secretary of Agriculture.

versions.research_rationale:
I read the complete held Federal Register original of Executive Order 8129 (4 FR 1997-1998, May 12, 1939; signed May 10, 1939): it reserves 144.30 acres in Benson County, North Dakota, for the use of the Department of Agriculture as the Minnewastena Migratory Waterfowl Refuge, makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture or disturb any bird or wild animal within the refuge or to enter it except under rules prescribed by the Secretary of Agriculture, and names the refuge. It has no duration, condition or sunset. I read the complete text of Public Land Order 1704 (23 FR 6110, Federal Register of August 9, 1958). Its title and operative paragraph revoke Executive Orders 8123, 8126, 8129 and 8163, which reserved lands for the Department of Agriculture as migratory waterfowl refuges, and it repeats the tract description of Executive Order 8129 (sec. 12, lot 7 and SW1/4SE1/4, and sec. 13, lot 1 and NW1/4NE1/4, T. 152 N., R. 65 W.). It is signed by the Assistant Secretary of the Interior on August 5, 1958, acting under Executive Order 10355, and has no partial limiter, exception or deferred effective date. That is the first end. The Federal Register disposition note dates the revocation August 4, 1958, but the order's own signature line reads August 5, 1958, so the held text controls. An earlier unnamed instrument, Reorganization Plan No. II of 1939 (section 4(f)), made effective July 1, 1939 by Public Resolution No. 20, transferred the Bureau of Biological Survey and wildlife functions from Agriculture to Interior. It does not name this order, so under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments it is recorded as a later event and a disclosed earlier candidate, not as the end. I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them: the U.S. Code search (through 2026-10-09) and the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found no citation of this order, and the disposition-note search found only the Public Land Order 1704 revocation. The Federal Register text layers are machine extracted and were checked only as text; the page images were not inspected.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order has no end date, condition, report deadline or sunset in its own words; the machine own-terms hit is the subject-to-valid-rights phrase, which is not a duration term. Candidates considered: (1) Reorganization Plan No. II of 1939, section 4(f), effective July 1, 1939 by the joint resolution approved June 7, 1939, which transferred Agriculture's wildlife and migratory-bird functions to Interior; it does not name this order and does not revoke the reservation or change its boundary, so it is disclosed as a later event and rejected as an end (the later revocation by Public Land Order 1704 itself recites reservation for the Department of Agriculture, which shows the reservation stayed on the books); (2) the catalog date of August 4, 1958, which the signature line of the public land order contradicts. Searches of the held order-text folders by number found only Public Land Order 1704 and the BLM editorial table of public land orders. No earlier named instrument and no held evidence of abandonment was found.","independent_command_check":"The prohibition on hunting, trapping, disturbing wildlife and entering the refuge, and the naming sentence, apply only within the reservation made by this order and fall with it; the order has no separate standing authority. The Secretary of Agriculture's power to prescribe rules is mentioned in the order, not created by it. No independent command of Executive Order 8129 remains after the revocation.","savings_check":"Public Land Order 1704 has no saving clause. It states that the lands are non-public lands, so no restoration or opening under the public-land laws follows. The valid-rights limit in the order protects pre-existing rights and is not a surviving effect of the order. Reorganization Plan No. II is not a residual of this order.","scope_check":"Public Land Order 1704 revokes the whole of Executive Order 8129: it lists the same tract described in the order, and it has no partial limiter or exception. The inventory is one clause from the first operative words to the sentence naming the refuge; it contains a Federal Register page-break line inside the text, which is page furniture and not an operative word. It also contains the heading-free closing sentence naming the refuge after the page break. The end date is the signature date, August 5, 1958; the public land order has no effective-date wording, and it was filed August 8 and published August 9, 1958, which are later dates and are not used."}

savings_residuals.reason: Public Land Order 1704 has no saving or exception clause for Executive Order 8129 and states that the lands are non-public lands, so it opens no land to entry under the public-land laws. No held source describes a pending proceeding or accrued right under this order. The order reserved the lands subject to valid rights, which protect rights that existed before the order and are not residual effects of it. Bounded searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Federal Register disposition notes found no surviving command.
